title: Selective metadata stripper and replay guard for console analytics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our console emits high-cardinality event payloads (user agents, filenames, command arguments, stack traces) into the analytics pipeline. Some fields are PII or sensitive for regulated customers. Current ad-hoc scrubbing is inconsistent across producers and downstream joins, causing compliance risk and customer requests for deletions/backfills.

Goal: Implement a centralized Selective Metadata Stripper service (SMS) plus a Replay Guard for safe developer debugging. SMS will apply field-level scrubbing policies at ingest and provide reversible, auditable access using timebound attestation keys only when explicit RBAC+auditor approval is granted. The Replay Guard controls replays of original payloads to safe sandboxes and enforces an audit trail.

Scope:
- Real-time ingestion integration (Kafka) with mobile/web/console clickstream and server telemetry topics.
- Two scrub modes: "ingest-first" (default: aggressive immutable strip) and "defer-scrub" (store encrypted raw blob with metadata tags and scrub on query/backfill).
- Deterministic pseudomask for identifiers (non-reversible) for analytics joins; reversible escrow for authorized investigations with ephemeral KMS-wrapped keys and attestation logs.
- Replay Guard service to gate replays of raw/enriched events to dev/test environments; requires auditor token and records who, why, and TTL.
- Backfill job to scrub historical raw events in storage per retention windows and legal requests.

Why unique: This ticket combines selective field stripping with an auditable reversible path (ephemeral keys + attestation) and a centralized replay guard, balancing compliance, developer troubleshooting, and analytics fidelity.
acceptance_criteria: SMS service is deployed behind the ingestion tier and can be toggled between ingest-first and defer-scrub per topic via config
Schema-driven policy engine applies field-level rules and emits sanitized events to analytics topics and masked-pseudonym IDs for joins
Reversible escrow path implemented: raw blob encrypted with customer-scoped key, access requires auditor approval and ephemeral key retrieval; access events recorded in audit log
Replay Guard blocks all non-approved replays of raw events to non-audited environments; approved replays leave persistent audit record
Backfill pipeline implemented to sanitize existing raw partitions and produces verifiable manifest of purged fields for compliance audits
E2E tests and canary rollout show <0.5% ingestion latency p50 increase and no data loss; cost impact and storage delta documented
implementation_notes:
Architecture: SMS sits as a consumer/producer between Kafka 'raw-events' and 'sanitized-events'. It uses an FK-based policy engine (config in S3 / console UI) and integrates with KMS/HSM for reversible escrow. Replay Guard is a separate service that validates auditor tokens via SSO and mints ephemeral role credentials for the consumer sandbox namespace.

Components & tech choices:
- Kafka consumer group + Beam streaming job for high-throughput low-latency transforms
- Policy engine coded in Go with WASM-based rule extensions for future-proofing
- Reversible escrow: envelope encryption with KMS; key-wrapping per-customer; audit events to immutable ledger (append-only S3 manifests)
- Backfill: Spark job with controlled concurrency and dry-run mode; emits manifest CSVs for legal-team ingestion
- Metrics: per-topic scrub-rate, redact-failure-rate, reversible-access-count, replay-requests, audit-log-index-latency

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged deploy to internal telemetry only (2 weeks)
2) Canary on non-sensitive customer topics (1 week)
3) Gradual topic-by-topic rollout with per-topic policy checks (4 weeks)
4) Run backfill for 90-day window, validate manifests with compliance team

Monitoring/SLOs: redact-failure-rate < 0.01%; ingestion p99 extra latency < 200ms; audit-log durability 99.999%; reversible-access TTLs expire reliably.

Security notes: All access to reversible blobs requires 2-step approval (auditor + manager). Detailed threat model attached in comments.
